src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
s: Headquarters of United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) is located in
x: UNEP (set up 1972) has its headquarters in Nairobi, Kenya – the first UN agency headquartered in the Global South. It is not in the USA (UN, UNDP, UNICEF – New York) or Germany (UNFCCC – Bonn).

s: FAO is the abbreviation of
x: FAO = Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN, headquartered in Rome, Italy (with IFAD and WFP); the other expansions are not real organisations.

s: The headquarters of IAAF is situated in
x: IAAF (International Association of Athletics Federations, renamed World Athletics in 2019) has been headquartered in Monaco; Switzerland hosts the IOC (Lausanne) and FIFA (Zurich), not athletics.

s: The Headquarters of the ‘Greenpeace International’ is located at :
x: Greenpeace International, the environmental NGO, is headquartered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands (legally Stichting Greenpeace Council); it began in Vancouver (Canada), which tempts the Ottawa option.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund?
x: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) has been IMF Managing Director since 1 October 2019 (second five-year term from October 2024), succeeding Christine Lagarde, who moved to the ECB. Jim Yong Kim was World Bank President; Joseph Stiglitz was World Bank chief economist.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund? 14.
x: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) has been IMF Managing Director since 1 October 2019 (second five-year term from October 2024), succeeding Christine Lagarde, who moved to the ECB. Jim Yong Kim was World Bank President; Joseph Stiglitz was World Bank chief economist.

s: INTERPOL stands for
x: INTERPOL = International Criminal Police Organization (founded 1923, HQ Lyon, France), commonly expanded as 'International Police Organisation'; it is not an Indian body.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) mainly works to
o: Promote global peace keeping and environment
Coordinate international environmental activities and policies
x: UNEP (1972, Nairobi) is the UN's global environmental authority: it coordinates international environmental activities and policies; it does not do peace-keeping, fund space research or build industries.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: What is not true about IFAD?
o: IFAD stands for International Fund for Agricultural Development
It is an agency working on hunger and poverty issues in rural areas in the developing countries
On 11 February 2020, the 43rd session of the governing council of IFAD was held at Berlin
It was the outcome of World Food Conference in 1974
x: Statement 3 is false: IFAD's 43rd Governing Council (11-12 February 2020) met in Rome, IFAD's headquarters city, not Berlin. IFAD (International Fund for Agricultural Development) arose from the 1974 World Food Conference and fights rural poverty and hunger in developing countries.

src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
s: Where is the Headquarters of North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)?
x: NATO (1949) is headquartered in Brussels (Haren), Belgium – the same city as the European Commission. Not to be confused with SHAPE (Mons).

s:
Which among the following countries got membership into BRICS bloc with effect from 1st January, 2024?

I. Egypt

II. Argentina

III. Indonesia

IV. Ethiopia

V. Saudi Arabia
x:
Most books and the key: Saudi Arabia joined on 1 Jan 2024 (I, IV, V). Strictly: Saudi Arabia was invited but has not formally confirmed membership (PMF IR p.115: 'with Saudi Arabia invited'; app notes 6:63 sub 5).
Invited at Johannesburg (Aug 2023), Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia were counted as joining from 1 January 2024; Argentina declined and Indonesia joined only in January 2025 – so I, IV and V.

s: Which of the following is the newest member of the Eurozone?
x:
the printed key Croatia (joined 1 Jan 2023) was right at the exam — now Bulgaria is the newest, 21st member from 1 Jan 2026 (Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 p.12).
Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, replacing the lev, and became the 21st euro-area member – now the newest (Croatia joined 1 January 2023; Lithuania 2015; Cyprus 2008).

s: Which of the following countries is not a member of SCO ?
x:
India became a full SCO member in June 2017 — now all four options are members (PMF IR p.93).
In 2013 India was only an SCO observer; China, Russia and Uzbekistan were full members (Uzbekistan from 2001). India (and Pakistan) became full members in 2017.

s: Which of the following countries was readmitted to the Common Wealth recently?
x: Pakistan, suspended from the Commonwealth after Musharraf's emergency rule (November 2007), was readmitted on 12 May 2008 by CMAG (it was also suspended 1999-2004). India and Bangladesh were never suspended; Nepal is not a member.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: In June 2022, which of the following countries became one of the latest members to join the Commonwealth?
x: Gabon (55th) and Togo (56th) joined the Commonwealth on 25 June 2022 at CHOGM Kigali – French-speaking states with no British colonial past, the first new members since Rwanda (2009). Cameroon joined 1995 and Ghana 1957.

s: In the Brexit referendum, the vote share of the group favouring exit and the group favouring remain was in the following ratio?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (52 : 48); it is added as option 5.
In the 23 June 2016 referendum Leave won 51.89% (17.41 million votes) and Remain 48.11% (16.14 million), i.e. about 52 : 48; every printed ratio (56:44 to 59:41) overstates the Leave margin. The UK left the EU on 31 January 2020.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following countries did not join the League of Nations?
x: The USA never joined the League of Nations: the Senate failed to ratify the Treaty of Versailles (1919-20) by the two-thirds majority, though President Wilson had proposed the League. China, British India and Cuba were founding members.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: What is the currency of Hungary?
x: Hungary's currency is the forint – it is an EU member (2004) but not in the euro area. Birr is Ethiopia's currency and real Brazil's.

s: Which of the following is not one of the UNESCO creative cities from India ?
x: India's UNESCO Creative Cities are Jaipur and Varanasi (2015), Chennai (2017), Mumbai and Hyderabad (2019), Srinagar (2021), Kozhikode (Literature) and Gwalior (Music) (2023) and Lucknow (Gastronomy, 2025). Pune is not one, so 'Pune (Literature)' is the odd one out.

s: In which country is the Angkorvat temple complex located?
x: Angkor Wat, the world's largest Hindu (later Buddhist) temple complex built by the Khmer king Suryavarman II, is in Cambodia, which was officially called Kampuchea (1975-89). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1992).

s: The brithplace of Christ is.
x: Tradition places the birth of Jesus Christ in Bethlehem (West Bank); the Church of the Nativity there is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012). Jerusalem is where he was crucified.

s:
With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements.

I. It is a song and dance performance.

II. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance.

III. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds Lord Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Manipuri Sankirtana is ritual singing, drumming and dancing that narrates the life and deeds of Krishna (I and III correct). II is wrong: the pung (drum) is central – 'usually performed by two drummers' – alongside cymbals. UNESCO ICH since 2013.

s: Which of the following was included in 2016 by UNESCO in the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
x: Yoga was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2016 (with Nawrouz). Vedic chanting and Ramlila were listed in 2008 and Sankirtana in 2013.

s: Which one of the following was the latest inclusion in the Intangible Cultural Heritage List of UNESCO? Indian Art and Culture PMF IAS IH – 239
x: Garba of Gujarat (December 2023) is the latest of these on UNESCO's ICH list; Chhau was listed in 2010, Kumbh Mela in 2017 and Durga Puja in Kolkata in 2021. (Since then Deepavali, December 2025, became India's 16th element – not an option.)

src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
s: In October 2019, which two Indian cities were included in UNESCO Create City Network?
x: Mumbai (Film) and Hyderabad (Gastronomy) were added to the UNESCO Creative Cities Network in October 2019; Bengaluru and Indore are not members, and Chennai was a 2017 Music city.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
s: India signed an MoU with South Africa for developing Youth Enterprises on ____
x: NSIC (Ministry of MSME) signed the MoU with South Africa's Black Business Council for youth-owned enterprises – five Rapid Incubation Centres – on 19 January 2015, in the presence of MSME Minister Kalraj Mishra.

s: Indian Union Cabinet approved the protocol to amend the DTAA (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement) with which Country in 2020?
x: On 12 February 2020 the Union Cabinet approved the Protocol amending the India–Sri Lanka DTAA (signed 2013) to add the BEPS Action 6 Principal Purpose Test, since Sri Lanka was not an MLI signatory.

s: India signed Mobility Pact with which Country?
x:
Official key: France (2018). Strictly: India has also signed such pacts with Germany (5 Dec 2022, bmi.bund.de), the UK (2021) and Italy (2023) — the UK and Italy from general knowledge, not checked — so the stem fits more than one option.
India's first Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement in Europe was signed with France in March 2018 (Macron's visit; ratified January 2020); it covers students, researchers and skilled professionals and irregular migration.

s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I (INTERPOL Notice)
List II (Description)
A. Silver Notice
1. To seek information on unidentified bodies
B. Blue Notice
2. To collect additional information about a person
C. Black Notice
3. To provide warning about criminal activities
D. Green Notice
4. To identify and trace criminal assets
Code:
x: Silver = identify and trace criminal assets (newest, 2025, pilot); Blue = collect additional information on a person's identity, location or activities; Black = information on unidentified bodies; Green = warning about a person's criminal activities (threat to public safety). So A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Recently, the United States of America (USA) and the European Union (EU) have launched the 'Trade and Technology Council'.
Statement-II: The USA and the EU claim that through this they are trying to bring technological progress and physical productivity under their control.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
x: Statement I is correct: the US-EU Trade and Technology Council was launched at the Brussels summit (15 June 2021) and first met in Pittsburgh (29 September 2021). Statement II is wrong: it aims to coordinate trade and technology policy and standards, not to bring technological progress and physical productivity 'under their control'. UPSC 2023 key (c).

s: According to INTERPOL, which State police had registered one of the first cases in India of human trafficking committed to force victims to commit cyber fraud?
x: INTERPOL's Operation Storm Makers II (late 2023) reported that police in Telangana registered one of India's first cases of human trafficking for the purpose of cyber fraud: an accountant lured to Southeast Asia was forced to run online scams and freed only after a ransom. The other States are not named in the INTERPOL release.

s: Which country was certified as Malaria-free by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024?
x: WHO certified Cabo Verde malaria-free on 12 January 2024 – the 43rd country and the 3rd in Africa after Mauritius (1973) and Algeria (2019). Mauritius (1973) and the other options were certified in earlier years, not 2024.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: When did the WHO member countries adopt a new International Treaty to enhance global co-ordination and co-operation on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response?
x: The 78th World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement on 20 May 2025 (Geneva) – the second health treaty under Art. 19 of the WHO Constitution after the FCTC (2003). The annex on pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) was left for further negotiation.

s: When was the first meeting of the United Nations Security Council held on the threats artificial intelligence poses to international peace and stability
x: The UN Security Council held its first-ever meeting on AI risks to international peace and security on 18 July 2023 (meeting 9381, chaired by UK Foreign Secretary James Cleverly during the UK presidency).

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: The United States reached an agreement to purchase Alaska from Russia in year:
x: Russia sold Alaska to the USA in 1867 (Treaty of Cession, $7.2 million, negotiated by Secretary of State William Seward); Alaska became the 49th US state in 1959.

s: Who is the Prime Minister of Italy as of 2024 ?
x: Giorgia Meloni (Brothers of Italy, centre-right) became Italy's first woman Prime Minister in October 2022, after the elections of 25 September 2022, and is still PM in 2026. Emma Bonino, Rosy Bindi and Laura Boldrini are Italian politicians who never held the post.
